subject: AcmeTech request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence
messages:
From: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@acmetech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+procurement@acmetech.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start drafting the SOW and run our internal resilience review, the architecture and procurement teams have a few follow-ups focused on your multi-region cutover guarantees and evidence. Can you share the following: 

- Clear RTO/RPO commitments (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with short notes on assumptions (replication lag, cache warming).
- A sanitized runbook or excerpt that shows the cutover sequence (region A -> region B) and the expected operator steps.
- Recent rehearsal evidence (logs or rehearsal report) that verifies timing for the last 2 rehearsals.
- Any required configuration or cost delta for geo-redundant reserved capacity and expected impact on throughput/latency.

We're on a tight timeline for procurement (target contract signature by end of month). If you can provide a short package and approximate cost delta, we'll take it into our review cycle. If needed, we can schedule a technical walk-through with your ops team.

Thanks,
Alyssa Moreno
Sr. Procurement Manager | AcmeTech
alyssa.moreno@acmetech.com

Attachment: acmetech-evidence-request.pdf (pdf, 74KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. High-level responses below; we'll assemble a sanitized evidence bundle and schedule a deep-dive with ops.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (shared): Target RTO 5m for stateless inference paths; RPO best-effort for non-persistent caches (we rely on prefix/KV cache rebuild).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): Target RTO 2-4m depending on sequence length & model variant; RPO & data replication is configurable — default is near-zero for persisted state (s3/replicated storage) and near-0 for metadata thanks to cross-AZ replication.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): RTO depends on customer infra; Redwood provides runbooks and orchestration hooks; typical validated RTO 2-6m in our private deployments during rehearsals.

Assumptions:
- RTO is measured from decision to cut traffic to first successful response from standby region.
- RPO pertains to persisted customer data (indexing, embeddings, logs). Ephemeral token-level caches may require warmup; we include cache-warmup strategies in the runbook.

Immediate next steps I'll take this afternoon:
1) Share a redactable runbook excerpt + the high-level failover sequence (attachment: regional-failover-commitment.pdf).
2) Provide sanitized rehearsal logs (we'll strip customer-sensitive content) — ETA 48 hours.
3) Provide a cost delta note for geo-redundant reserved capacity (ballpark) and a short list of config flags you need to enable.

Propose a 30-min technical review at 10:00am PT on Thursday (Aug 6) to walk through runbook and evidence. Let me know if that works.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: regional-failover-commitment.pdf (pdf, 112KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence

Adding a few technical clarifications to make the evidence pack useful to Acme's architects: 

- Cutover sequence (short):
  1) Pause ingress to region A for affected routes (seconds).
  2) Flush or snapshot local KV cache to persistent store (if customer opts in).
  3) Switch routing policy -> region B; warm caches with KV prefix cache if required.
  4) Verify model and tokenizer variants are consistent; confirm KV cache hits reach steady-state.
  5) Resume full traffic and monitor tail-latency & error rates.

- Cache warmup: Our automated warmup uses a prioritized prefix replay up to a configured token budget (typically 1-5% of daily token volume) — this is what drives the discrepancy between RTO and end-to-end latency normalization. We'll document expected time-to-steady-state for sample payloads.

- Data replication: Persisted artifacts (embeddings, logs) replicate cross-region via cloud object-store replication and transactionally applied metadata in the control plane. For low-RPO needs we recommend enabling synchronous replication for critical artifacts — call this out in the runbook.

Evidence we'd include: rehearsal-scan1.log (sanitized), rehearsal-summary-20260612.pdf, failover-runbook-snippet.md, config-diff-geo-enabled.json (redacted). Any legal/SOC statements should be pulled from the Compliance team; I'll ask Security for a SOC2 coverage statement we can include as a signed PDF.

Marissa/KT: can you confirm whether we should include the cache-warmup timing table for the 1M token sample (it helps procurement quantify client impact)?

-Markus

From: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@acmetech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmetech.com>, ops+procurement@acmetech.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence

Thanks Karthik and Markus — that looks promising. A few quick asks so procurement and our SREs can move forward: 

- Please provide a formalized evidence pack (PDF bundle) with:
  * sanitized rehearsal logs showing timestamps for each stage of the cutover,
  * the runbook excerpt showing operator commands and expected checks,
  * a short table that maps the RTO/RPO numbers to the configuration flags we must enable.
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a fixed SLA clause for RTO (e.g., targeted 4m for dedicated with a <5% exceptions allowance per quarter) or whether this is only an operational target?
- Procurement needs an order-of-magnitude cost delta for geo redundancy (monthly), plus any on-call support hours you recommend for the first 3 rehearsals.

We can take a sanitized package into our architecture review next week. If possible, please include the SOC2 coverage statement; if Security needs to vet redactions, we can treat the sanitized files as confidential.

If you can get the sanitized bundle and a short cost note before EOD Thursday we'll route it to legal and procurement.

Best,
Alyssa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region cutover scenarios, RTO/RPO evidence

Alyssa — attached is the initial sanitized evidence pack and a short commercial note. Highlights: 

- Evidence pack (attachments): sanitized-rehearsal-logs.zip (contains rehearsal-scan1.log, rehearsal-scan2.log with timestamps and stage markers), failover-runbook-snippet.md, rehearsal-summary-20260612.pdf, SOC2-coverage-statement.pdf (redacted cover page).
- SLA language: Redwood treats the RTO as a contractual SLA only for Dedicated Reserved Capacity under a specific SOW/addendum. We can offer a targeted 4-minute SLA with a 5% quarterly exception allowance as an addendum; I'll route the DocuSign envelope for procurement if you confirm.
- Commercial: Geo-redundant reserved capacity typically adds ~5-8% to monthly committed cost depending on pool sizing and burst policy. Estimated monthly delta for the footprint discussed in the POC: $8,500–$12,000 (ballpark). Exact pricing requires final capacity sizing.
- Ops support recommendation: 8 hours of Redwood on-call assistance spread across first 3 rehearsals; we can bake that into onboarding as a one-time services line item.

Links & next steps: 
- Evidence (sanitized): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD9-runbook-sanitized
- DocuSign: envelope-0a1b2c3d4e (SLA addendum draft)
- Proposed review: Thu Aug 6, 10:00am PT (confirm) — we'll use the runbook excerpt to walk through each stage and the rehearsal timestamps.

If you confirm the review slot, I'll include Security on the call to answer SOC2 scope questions and to agree on redaction approach for the final evidence bundle.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
